question: What is the primary purpose of patient education on drug use?

options.A: To reduce the workload of hospital pharmacists
options.B: To bridge clinical prescription and safe home administration
options.C: To eliminate all potential side effects of medications
options.D: To replace verbal doctor consultations completely

explanation: Education ensures that patients understand how to take their prescribed drugs safely once they leave the healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why must nurses evaluate a patient's health literacy before teaching?

options.A: To determine the financial cost of the prescribed drugs
options.B: To decide if the patient needs admission to the ward
options.C: To choose the most effective and appropriate communication method
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital administrative paperwork

explanation: Understanding literacy levels allows nurses to tailor their language and teaching tools so the patient actually comprehends the instructions. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h1)

question: The correct route of administration tells the patient what?

options.A: How long the entire treatment course will last
options.B: What time of day the medication must be purchased
options.C: How the drug should enter or be applied to the body
options.D: Which pharmacy stocks the specific brand of drug

explanation: Route specifies whether a drug is swallowed, injected, applied topically, or inhaled. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient asks why they must finish a full five-day antibiotic course even after feeling better. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Remaining pills can be saved for future common illnesses
options.B: The hospital policy requires all drug bottles to be emptied
options.C: Unfinished medications react badly with household storage
options.D: Stopping early allows stronger bacteria to survive and return

explanation: Instructing patients on duration prevents drug resistance and relapse of the infection. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h2)

question: A major barrier to patient education in many Nigerian clinical settings is what?

options.A: Patients refusing to ask any questions during ward rounds
options.B: Doctors forbidding nurses from talking about prescriptions
options.C: Language differences between clinical terms and local dialects
options.D: Excessive availability of translated drug package inserts

explanation: The gap between formal medical English and local languages often requires careful translation by the nurse. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h3)

question: How can a nurse minimize the barrier of medical jargon during patient teaching?

options.A: By using simple, everyday language instead of technical terms
options.B: By speaking much faster to cover all points quickly
options.C: By handing out advanced medical textbooks for home study
options.D: By writing instructions only in Latin abbreviations

explanation: Replacing complex medical terms with common words helps patients grasp vital instructions without confusion. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why do many patients with chronic illnesses stop taking their prescribed drugs?

options.A: Pharmacists advise them to take drug holidays every weekend
options.B: Chronic drugs lose all their chemical potency after a month
options.C: Hospitals routinely stop supplying medications after one week
options.D: They feel better and mistakenly assume the disease is cured

explanation: Asymptomatic chronic conditions often lead patients to believe treatment is no longer necessary. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h4)

question: What practical advice should a nurse give a patient for storing medicines in a hot climate?

options.A: Keep medications in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight
options.B: Store all fragile tablet bottles inside the household cooking pot
options.C: Keep liquid suspensions sitting directly under outdoor sunlight
options.D: Leave medication packs on the car dashboard for easy access

explanation: Heat and humidity degrade chemical compounds in medications, making proper storage vital. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which symptom indicates a severe adverse drug reaction requiring immediate medical attention?

options.A: Temporary loss of appetite on the first treatment day
options.B: Mild drowsiness occurring an hour after taking a pill
options.C: Slight change in urine color after taking vitamins
options.D: Sudden facial swelling and difficulty breathing

explanation: Facial swelling and breathing difficulty are classic signs of anaphylaxis or severe hypersensitivity. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is it important to warn patients about expected mild side effects beforehand?

options.A: To ensure they buy extra medications to treat the side effects
options.B: To prevent panic and stop them from abandoning treatment
options.C: To prove that the prescribed drug is working very fast
options.D: To comply with legal rules against selling potent drugs

explanation: Knowing what to expect stops patients from abruptly stopping necessary therapy due to fear. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary benefit of the teach-back method during patient education?

options.A: It replaces the need to write down any prescription labels
options.B: It confirms whether the patient truly comprehends the instructions
options.C: It tests the patient's long-term memory for past illnesses
options.D: It measures the exact physical strength of the patient

explanation: Having patients repeat instructions in their own words exposes any misunderstandings before they leave. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable way to verify patient comprehension?

options.A: Asking the patient to demonstrate how they will use an inhaler
options.B: Using the teach-back method to check clarity of instructions
options.C: Asking the closed-ended question 'Do you understand?'
options.D: Asking the patient to repeat the dosing schedule out loud

explanation: Closed questions usually prompt automatic polite nods without verifying actual understanding. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h6)
